title: Trade History shows every buy and sell time as a date in January 1970: the API sends Unix seconds and the table passes them to new Date() as milliseconds

evidence.note: buyTime / sellTime are trades.buy_time / sell_time (Unix seconds); durationHeld is their difference in seconds
the CSV export of the same fields multiplies by 1000 before new Date(), confirming the unit
contrast: the positions table treats buyTime as seconds (Date.now() / 1000 - buyTime)

sibling_sites_checked: Every time rendering in the dashboard: TradeTable formatDate (this finding); PositionTable time held (seconds, correct); formatTimeAgo for notifications, anti-rug events, CB triggers and heartbeats (all produced with Date.now() in milliseconds: broadcaster.ts:42, exitTrigger.ts:140, detector.ts:1074, circuitBreaker.ts:106; correct); PauseBanner pausedAt (seconds, multiplied by 1000, correct); TradeHistory range filter (ISO date, correct); formatDuration of durationHeld (seconds, correct).
severity_rationale: S3: the trade history is the operator's record of when positions were opened and closed; every row shows a 1970 date, so ordering by eye and matching against chain explorers or logs is impossible from the dashboard. No money path.
recommendation: Multiply by 1000 in formatDate (or send milliseconds and say so in the type). Phase 29.
